Plot a goal from its tracking

Source: R/plot.R
plot_goal.Rd

plot_goal() draws every skater, both goalies and the puck at one frame (by default the moment it went in), each with the path he skated over the trail seconds before, and the puck's path. plot_goal_sequence() draws n frames leading up to the goal, side by side.

Usage

plot_goal(frames, frame = NULL, trail = 2, title = NULL)

plot_goal_sequence(frames, n = 6, seconds = 5, title = NULL)

Arguments

frames

Tracking frames from nhl_goal_tracking().

frame

The frame to draw; NULL for the goal (goal_frame()).

trail

Seconds of path behind each player and the puck.

title

Plot title; NULL for the game and event ids.

n

Number of frames.

seconds

How far before the goal the sequence starts.

Value

A ggplot.

Examples

path <- system.file("extdata", "goal-2025020534-777.json.gz", package = "bluelineR")
frames <- read_goal_tracking(path, 2025020534, 777)
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  plot_goal(frames, title = "McDavid, shorthanded breakaway at Boston")
}
